title: Officer said he was stabbed: Inquiry witness describes scene of fatal police shooting: [Early Edition]
article: A shaken, blood-splattered Calgary police officer reached under Deng Fermino Kuol's lifeless body and pulled free a small knife as he explained to a bystander, "He stabbed me," a fatality inquiry heard Thursday.

Several residents of a southeast apartment building testified that Const. Ira Macumber appeared to be in shock with the colour drained from his face as he crouched in a hallway moments after shooting Kuol twice in the neck on Oct. 25, 2003, provincial court Judge Gerald Meagher heard.

The shooting happened after police were called to remove Kuol, who refused to leave an apartment building in the 1700 block of 37th Street S.E. An intoxicated Kuol allegedly slashed the officer, who fired in self-defence.
Macumber is expected to take the stand today.
Other inquiry witnesses testified that Kuol was falling-down drunk and sleeping in a stairwell that night.
Tenants Susan Jordan and her boyfriend Roger Burr both spoke with Macumber right after the shooting.
Jordan heard the officer call out that he'd been stabbed. Burr got halfway down the building's front staircase when he saw Kuol's limp body.
"(Macumber) was sitting against the wall holding his arm," recalled Burr.
The truck driver then asked Macumber if he was OK or needed help, but didn't get a response.
"I looked in his eyes and there was no colour in them," said Burr. "I don't think he knew what happened, he just knew it happened."

Jordan ran to the officer's side after hearing two gunshots. She said she could smell gunpowder as she came down the stairs, and that Macumber reached under Kuol's body, producing a small paring or steak knife. "He stabbed me," the officer said, according to Jordan.

The shooting, said Burr, was the finale to a long and drawn-out saga involving Kuol and his two friends living in apartment No. 1 in the basement. Kuol had been asked to leave more than once after being discovered sleeping in the stairwell, Jordan said. There was always fighting, loud music and copious amounts of drinking, court heard.

Gabriel Mbataboro, whose apartment Kuol visited hours before he was shot dead, testified Kuol was so drunk he fell off a chair and was asked to leave because he was getting too loud. "I do not believe he was capable of struggling with that officer," said Mbataboro.
Freda Bastien had lived in No. 1 for only five days before the shooting. She met Kuol in the spring of 1999 in Brooks and knew him to be a violent drunk.
Bastien testified Kuol came to her apartment four times on the day of the shooting, but she refused to let him in.
On his final visit, Bastien's Sudanese roommates called the police to say Kuol was passed out at their door. An almost-empty bottle of Big Bear beer was at Kuol's side, she said.
It was less than 20 minutes later when Macumber arrived at the apartment and said he would take care of the situation. Bastien went back to watching TV while her roommates went to bed.
"I could hear the police officer talking to Fermino, three or four times asking him to put out his cigarette," she said.
Macumber, she testified, was "sort of calm."
"He seemed to be fine. He wasn't harsh or rude to (Kuol)," she said.
But the conversation between the two men didn't last long. Within seconds, Bastien heard a "scuffle" outside the door. She looked out the peephole and witnessed the two men on the nearby staircase.
"When I opened the door, I saw the police officer with the gun and that's when he shot Fermino," she said. "For me, what it looked like was he shot him in the neck."
Bastien, who said she was calm during the incident, watched as Macumber fumbled to get his gun back in its holster. He started muttering to himself.
"'Oh my God. Oh my God.' He said it three or four times," Bastien said of Macumber's reaction. "He was trying to handcuff Fermino, but he was having a hard time."
Bastien said she didn't actually witness the two men struggle, nor did she see Kuol with a knife.

Kuol, 34, came to Calgary in 1997 after escaping wartorn Sudan. The court heard Kuol was convicted three times in Brooks for assaulting co-workers at Lakeside Packers slaughterhouse. He was also convicted of beating his girlfriend.
